card.title: Old Reflex
card.instruction: Turn to this person first whenever uncertainty appears, as an old reflex. Notice the habit only after you have already involved them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which key opens my new flat? Sorry, you haven't been there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Which pocket would I have put the key in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your left, usually. Put a hook by the door so you won't need to ring me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There it is. How high should the hook go? You've never seen the door. I'll send you a photo.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks about an unseen flat before noticing the habit, A3 asks about the pocket, and A5 recruits B into hook placement before again noticing the knowledge gap.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's independent-flat reminder shifts A3 to a familiar pocket; B4's hook solution creates A5's next reflexive consultation.

relationship.evidence: B2 notes the new independence and B4 gives both useful personal knowledge and a practical way to reduce calls.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's independence aid as the next reason to involve B, then recognizes and repairs the missing visual context.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a new flat and lost key location; B4 supplies the usual left pocket.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's photo offer follows the self-caught door question, showing rather than naming the persistent reflex.
